solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: From part of empire, perhaps: no one local, sadly

indicators.note: things that go sadly go badly wrong, so the letters end up in a disordered state

parts.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone from a far corner of an empire laments that no local person is around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' becomes the numeral I before the rearranging, so the fodder is eight letters, not the ten of the words as printed.
explanation.definitionFit: A colony is a territory belonging to an empire, and colonial describes a person or thing coming from such a territory.

clue.text: Female compatriot of noble line without husband

parts.note: a count is a European nobleman
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line
W/O is the written abbreviation for without
as in 'man and wife'

explanation.surface: A woman from a noble family who has no husband is described as a fellow citizen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without husband' reads as a woman being unmarried, but 'without' is the shorthand W/O and 'husband' supplies letters of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: A compatriot is someone from your own country, and the female form of countryman names a woman sharing that nationality.

clue.text: Dangerous reptile descending on American plant

indicators.note: in a down clue, something that descends on another comes down to sit above it

parts.note: short for crocodile
US is the standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A crocodile swoops down on some American vegetation.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second, which is what 'descending on' describes.
explanation.definitionFit: The crocus is a small flowering bulb that blooms in early spring, a familiar garden example of a plant.

clue.text: Charlie conceals rebukes

parts.note: Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
to conceal is to hide

explanation.surface: A man called Charlie hides reprimands he has been given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conceals' looks like a container signal, but here it simply supplies a synonym placed after the single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To chide someone is to scold or reprimand them mildly, a straightforward synonym for this verb form.

clue.text: Last part is false — authentic originally

parts.note: cod is an informal adjective meaning fake or mock, as in a cod accent

indicators.note: what something is originally is how it starts, so only an opening letter is kept

parts.note: its opening letter

explanation.surface: Someone complains that the ending of a story is fake, though it started out genuine.
explanation.walkthrough: Cod meaning 'sham' is a British informal usage worth knowing: a cod accent is a put-on one.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is the concluding passage of a piece of music or literary work, so it names a final section.

clue.text: Scoundrel keeping Oscar, behold in the shade

indicators.note: to keep something is to hold it inside, so one piece wraps around the others

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible man
Oscar is O in the NATO phonetic alphabet
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: A villain lurks in the shadows holding on to an Oscar statuette, and we are told to look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The shade' sounds like shadow, but shade here is a tint; 'in the' only links it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A shade is a particular variety of hue, so it serves as a direct synonym for a tint or hue.

clue.text: Fashionable Post Office, one found by river naturally

parts.note: hip means trendy
the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A trendy post office stands, as you would expect, beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a playful description: hippopotamus means 'river horse', and it lives in and by African rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: Hippopotamuses spend their days wallowing in African rivers, so a creature found by water in the wild fits them exactly.

clue.text: Coy Bill plays daft: not like these words!

indicators.note: playing daft means acting foolishly, so the letters behave in a silly, disordered way

parts.note: the letters as printed

explanation.surface: A shy man named Bill pretends to be foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: Every word in the clue has a single syllable, so the definition points back at the clue itself: its words are the opposite of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue is written entirely in one-syllable words, and the answer describes words having many syllables, their exact opposite.

clue.text: Grain seen reflected in moonrock

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the letters run the other way
something seen within a phrase is visible there already, waiting to be picked out

parts.note: the letters running across the middle of the word

explanation.surface: Particles glinting in a lunar rock sample catch the light.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside a single word, backwards; 'reflected' suits the surface's shiny moonrock.
explanation.definitionFit: Corn is a general word for cereal crops such as wheat or maize, and their seeds are grain.

clue.text: Rotter I ring to return luxury car

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man
taken as written

indicators.note: to return is to go back the way you came, so these letters run backwards

parts.note: to ring is to call on the telephone

explanation.surface: A bounder asks to be phoned so he can bring back an expensive motor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' tempts as the letter O, but it is the verb to telephone; 'rotter' and 'cad' are old-fashioned British words for a scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadillac is an American brand of expensive, prestigious automobiles, so its name is an example of a high-end vehicle.

clue.text: Curtsies afresh, serving oranges, say

indicators.note: doing something afresh means making it anew, so the letters are formed again differently

parts.note: the letters as printed

explanation.surface: A waitress bobs down again as she hands round the oranges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serving' belongs to the waiting-staff picture but only joins wordplay to definition here; 'say' marks oranges as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: Oranges belong to the citrus family along with lemons and limes, so they are examples of that fruit group.

clue.text: Girl only feet from the TV, immobile

indicators.note: feet are at the bottom of a body, so only the final letter of each word is kept

parts.note: the tail letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A girl sits motionless with her feet just in front of the television.
explanation.walkthrough: TV counts as a word here, so its closing V is one of the three letters taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Eve is a female first name, and crosswords often define a name simply by the kind of person bearing it.

clue.text: Brief detailed description you gamble on?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a clipped form of specification
second meaning: a clipped form of speculation, a risky purchase

explanation.walkthrough: Both meanings are clipped forms of longer words; the question mark flags the looser second sense, from the phrase 'on spec'.
explanation.definitionFit: The short form stands for specification, a precise technical outline, and for speculation, a risky venture undertaken hoping for profit.

clue.text: Long poem cut by half causes widespread ill-feeling

indicators.note: a thing cut by something has that something driven into it, splitting it apart

parts.note: an epic is a long narrative poem
demi- is a prefix meaning half

explanation.surface: Chopping a lengthy poem in half makes people widely resentful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ill-feeling' suggests resentment, but read literally it is feeling ill: widespread sickness.
explanation.definitionFit: An epidemic is an outbreak of disease affecting many people at once, literally sickness spread over a population.

clue.text: Cry of rook perhaps, possessing large talon

indicators.note: to possess is to have and hold, so one piece holds another inside it

parts.note: the harsh call of a crow or rook
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A bird's cry comes from a creature with an enormous hooked nail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rook' could be the chess piece, but 'perhaps' marks it as an example of a bird whose call is the familiar crow's croak.
explanation.definitionFit: A talon is the sharp hooked nail of a bird of prey, a specific kind of the curved nail on an animal's foot.

clue.text: As copper, for example, call time after disturbance

indicators.note: a disturbance throws things into disarray, so the letters come out jumbled

parts.note: the letters as printed

explanation.surface: A police officer, say, ends the drinking session after a fracas in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' is British slang for a police officer, and 'call time' is what a pub landlord does at closing; here copper is just a metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper is one of the metals, so something described as being like copper is of the nature of metal.

clue.text: Measuring system encountered, endlessly valuable

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is dropped off

parts.note: to encounter is to meet, past tense
rich, meaning valuable, loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone came across a system of measurement that is of limitless worth.
explanation.walkthrough: Rich here means of great worth, as in rich treasures.
explanation.definitionFit: Metric, as a noun, is a standard of measurement, and the metric system is the decimal set of units.

clue.text: Sailor with waterproof coat found on road

parts.note: tar is an old word for a sailor
short for mackintosh, a raincoat

explanation.surface: A seaman in a raincoat turns up on the highway.
explanation.walkthrough: A mac is the British word for a raincoat.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarmac is the hard surfacing laid on streets, and by extension names a paved roadway or runway itself.

clue.text: Reduce run for one travelling to work

parts.note: to commute a sentence is to reduce it
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: Someone cuts back on their jogging in favour of the trip to the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reduce' uses the legal sense: commuting a sentence lessens the punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: A commuter makes a regular journey between home and a place of employment, so the phrase describes them directly.

clue.text: Oil exporters work with European Community

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
the standard abbreviation

explanation.surface: Petroleum-selling nations cooperate with Europe's trading bloc.
explanation.walkthrough: Opus is the Latin for work, used for numbered musical compositions.
explanation.definitionFit: OPEC is the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries, a cartel of nations that sell crude to the world.

clue.text: Boy having beer cold

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
C is the tap abbreviation for cold

explanation.surface: A lad is drinking a chilled beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boy' in crosswords usually means any male first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Alec is a male first name, and crossword setters routinely clue names by the kind of person bearing them.

clue.text: Genning up: it regularly leads to boredom

indicators.note: at regular intervals means every other letter is taken in steady steps

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: Studying hard to get informed only ends in tedium.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Genning up' is British slang for acquiring information; start with the second letter, not the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a French borrowing for listless weariness and dissatisfaction, a close synonym for that dull state.

clue.text: Ace detectives in charge becoming sour

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for ace on playing cards
the Criminal Investigation Department, the British police detective branch
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: Top detectives given command turn bitter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ace' looks like an adjective praising the detectives, but it is a card giving one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Acidic describes a sharp, tart taste like lemon juice or vinegar, a straightforward synonym for this adjective.
